claim: A pull-based cold copy of a checkpoint session tree is crash-consistent and restores exactly on the same lane: generations are immutable, SHA-manifested, and atomically published.

steps.detail: allowlisted session tree, WSL ext4 -> drvfs staging -> SMB (sync script), byte-verified 9 files / 5,042,999,375 bytes
NAS -> drvfs staging over site-to-site WAN at ~28.3 MB/s (~3 min)
staging -> local ext4 store, root-owned 0700 like container writes
checkpoint status served from the installed copy: same generation, frontier 67935, read_backend io_uring-odirect
docker restart of the released production container
previous_response_id from the copied manifest: HTTP 200, reuse=private_endpoint, cache=67935 restored, server ttft 0.58 s, wall 15.8 s (disk restore dominates)

caveats: Restore is runtime-fingerprint-bound: a copied tree resumes only on an identical lane pair (same binary, artifact, config).

The engine refuses restore while the session is still live in its index (correct: never clobber resident state) - the drill therefore models recovery after process loss; the pre-restart attempt 404s by design when the response store has evicted the record.
Released v0.4.0 store semantics: quota must hold two generations of a session during a save transition; production runs 24576 MiB. The v0.4.1 tolerance fix (ninfer#27) removes that sizing constraint.
Replication policy: allowlisted public-safe sessions only; secret-bearing sessions stay local per the fleet security classes.
